label: Web Agency
register: The buyer is a small or mid-sized business owner deciding whether this local agency looks skilled and trustworthy enough to build and market their website, judged against other modern web design and digital marketing studios rather than solo freelancers or large enterprise consultancies.

sites.name: Digital Silk
sites.why: Leads with a short growth-focused promise and a single 'get a proposal' action, then immediately backs it with big-client logos, award badges and case-study results rather than a service list.

sites.name: Big Drop
sites.why: Portfolio-first homepage: large full-bleed project visuals do the selling, with a location-specific headline (NYC web design) and review-platform ratings as trust signals.

sites.name: Clay
sites.why: Confident minimal hero with oversized type and a recognisable client logo wall, then large case-study cards; restraint signals senior design skill.

sites.name: Ramotion
sites.why: Each case study is framed around a measurable outcome (e.g. a percentage improvement) with the client name, so proof is quantified rather than claimed.

sites.name: Flow Ninja
sites.why: Positions around one clear specialism (Webflow partner) with named enterprise clients and a 'how we work' model section, showing expertise through focus rather than a long list of services.

sites.name: Bop Design
sites.why: Mid-sized agency that speaks directly to a defined audience (B2B companies) and pairs a clear niche headline with years in business and review ratings, a realistic model for a local agency.
